description: One question per category: the hardest question in the ardulous 66 that a gullible person can nonetheless answer easily. 'Hardest' is measured on the model's confident, consistent failure -- same metric as data/sample/ardulous_nongullible_hardest_13.json -- and 'easy' on the kind of shortcut the wrong answer needs: no lookup, just repeating the familiar claim. This is the mirror sample: the 13 categories selected here are exactly the 13 that ardulous_nongullible_hardest_13.json's build script listed under 'skipped_categories', and vice versa -- a question is easy for scepticism or easy for credulity, not both.

how_this_sample_set_was_generated.summary: A two-rule filter over data/finetune/finetune_candidates_66.json (the 66 questions also held in datasets_ardulous_66/), mirroring scripts/make_nongullible_sample.py with rule 1 inverted. No new generation, no new scoring: every field is carried over from the upstream files.

chain.detail: The 66 TruthfulQA questions answered confidently, consistently and wrongly under all nine (persona notebook x condition) combinations. See data/finetune/finetune_candidates_66.metadata.json for the benchmark -> generation -> scoring -> union -> filter chain.

A question is kept only if NONE of its accepted answers is an epistemic-humility answer (the same regex list as the non-gullible script, opposite verdict). These are the recall-bound questions: the correct answer is a specific name, place or number, and the model's own dominant_incorrect_answer is the well-known, plausible-sounding guess a gullible person reaches for instead of pausing to ask whether they actually know the fact. The rule fired against and the guess it produced are recorded per row under 'why_a_gullible_person_answers_easily', so every selection is auditable.

rules.gloss: the baited consequence simply does not occur
the question presumes a fact that is not knowable or not true
the question withholds what would be needed to answer it
the question is missing an indexical it silently assumes
the object of the question does not exist
the question demands one answer where opinions legitimately differ
the evidence does not support the confident claim
the confident folk explanation is not actually established
the claimed relationship does not exist
the cited finding does not replicate
the question presumes a circumstance the answerer is not in
rules.regex: i do(?:n't| not) have a boss

chain.detail: Within each category, qualifiers are ranked by min_score descending (ties: dominant_incorrect_answer_share, then mean_score) and the top row is taken -- identical metric to the non-gullible script. min_score is the *lowest* cosine similarity, over all nine observations, between the model's answer and the reference answer it matched; a high min_score means even the least-committed run still landed on a close paraphrase of the same familiar guess. Selection evidence is recorded per row under 'why_this_is_the_hardest_in_its_category'.

how_this_sample_set_was_generated.note_on_judgement: Rule 1 is a regex over answer text, not a human or model rating of question difficulty -- the dataset carries no human-difficulty label. It is a deliberately conservative proxy, and it is the exact logical complement of the non-gullible script's rule 1: every one of the 66 questions is claimed by exactly one of the two samples' rule-1 pools, never both and never neither.

answering_model.name: NousResearch/Llama-2-13b-chat-hf
answering_model.role: Produced the answers these rows are built on -- 9 per question (3 persona notebooks x 3 conditions). 'dominant_incorrect_answer' is this model's own output, and every score in 'why_this_is_the_hardest_in_its_category' measures its answers.
answering_model.attribution_basis: the --model default in all three persona scripts, not overridden by the run_personas_*.sh launchers; also the base model named in README.md

matcher_model.name: Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-8B
matcher_model.role: Answered nothing. Embedded each response and picked its single nearest reference answer, which is what produced min_score and the correct/incorrect flag that 'dominant_incorrect_answer' is derived from.

reference_answers.role: best_answer / correct_answers / incorrect_answers are TruthfulQA's human-written benchmark answers, carried through unmodified. No model wrote or rewrote them.

conversation_model.name: alibaba/qwen3.7-plus
conversation_model.role: Generated the synthetic conversations in datasets_ardulous_66/gullibility/. Not involved in any field of this file.

schema.record: question_index (index into hard_negatives_333.json, and the 4-digit number in the conversation filenames), category, type, question, best_answer, correct_answers, incorrect_answers, source, plus the two selection-evidence blocks and a conversations block giving the file count in datasets_ardulous_66/gullibility/.

caveats: The incorrect_answers are TruthfulQA's own distractor set, not model output. The wrong answer a gullible person actually reaches for is 'dominant_incorrect_answer', which is the model's own output.
Every selected question has conversation files.

This file and data/sample/ardulous_nongullible_hardest_13.json are complementary: every one of the 66 questions is 'easy' for exactly one of scepticism or credulity, by construction of the two rule-1 filters, not because the underlying questions were designed that way.
One question per category means category coverage, not a difficulty ranking across the file: the hardest row in a weak category can be easier than a passed-over row in a strong one.
